```{r setup}
library(rxs2tria)
```

Preparing a dataset is often iterative: data processing reveals issues
in the raw data, images are re-analysed in ROXAS or ROXAS AI, images are
added or removed, or the dataset is built up in parts (e.g. one site
at a time) and combined for submission. The `update_*()` and
`combine_*()` functions handle these cases without repeating the
completed steps of the `vignette("workflow")`.

| Situation | Functions |
|---|---|
| Images re-analysed, output files replaced | `update_QWAimages()`, `update_QWAdata()`, `update_QWAmetadata()` |
| Images added to or removed from the dataset | `combine_QWAimages()` or a filter, then `update_QWAdata()`, `update_QWAmetadata()` |
| Datasets prepared separately, e.g. per site | `combine_QWAimages()`, `combine_QWAdata()`, `combine_QWAmetadata()` |

The `QWAimages` object defines the images of the dataset: update it
first, then the `QWAdata` and `QWAmetadata` objects to match it.

The objects below follow the names of the workflow: `rxs_images`
(`QWAimages`), `QWA_data` (`QWAdata`) and `QWA_meta` (`QWAmetadata`).

## Re-analysed images

If data processing reveals issues in the raw data and you re-analyse
one or more images with ROXAS or ROXAS AI:

1. Replace the output files in `path_in` with the newly generated files.
2. Re-read the settings/metadata for those images in the `QWAimages`
   object (no need to repeat Steps 1 and 2 of the workflow):

```{r}
rxs_images <- update_QWAimages(rxs_images,
  imgs_to_reread = c("IMAGELABEL1", "IMAGELABEL2"),
  settings_date_orders = settings_date_orders) # as in Step 3 (ROXAS only)
# if a QWAmetadata object exists, update it as well (keeps the values
# entered in the metadata app):
# QWA_meta <- update_QWAmetadata(QWA_meta, rxs_images)
```

3. Update the `QWAdata` object. For the re-read images, the raw cells
   and rings files are read again, and derived measures and automatic
   flags are recalculated. By default, any manual edits made in the
   flags app for these images are also reset. Set
   `reset_manual_flags = FALSE` to keep them only if the re-analysis was
   minor and the dating was not affected:

```{r}
QWA_data <- update_QWAdata(QWA_data, meta = rxs_images,
  imgs_to_reread = c("IMAGELABEL1", "IMAGELABEL2"))
```

4. Review `only_ew` and `img_comment` of the re-analysed images in the
   metadata app, e.g. a comment noting that the image needs re-analysis.

`update_QWAdata()` recalculates the duplicate-ring flags for all
woodpiece-years with a re-read image, as overlaps may change. The
re-read images are new data: inspect their flags again in the flags app
or re-apply any custom rule for `exclude_issues`.

## Added or removed images

To add images, there are two options:

- Rerun Steps 1--3 of the workflow on the updated `path_in` to rebuild
  `rxs_images`. Any `only_ew` and `img_comment` values entered in the
  metadata app are then missing from `rxs_images`
  (`update_QWAmetadata()` below fills them in).
- Run Steps 1--3 on a separate folder containing only the new images to
  obtain `rxs_images_new`, and combine it with the existing object. This
  keeps existing values. Both objects must have the same ROXAS version
  and distinct image labels:

```{r}
rxs_images <- combine_QWAimages(rxs_images, rxs_images_new)
```

To remove images, filter them from `rxs_images`:

```{r}
rxs_images <- rxs_images |>
  dplyr::filter(!image_label %in% c("IMAGELABEL1", "IMAGELABEL2"))
```

Then update the `QWAdata` object. Images new in `rxs_images` are read
and added, images no longer in `rxs_images` are removed, and the
duplicate-ring flags are recalculated for all affected woodpiece-years:

```{r}
QWA_data <- update_QWAdata(QWA_data, meta = rxs_images)
```

If a `QWAmetadata` object exists, update it as well. This replaces its
images and adds or removes the corresponding rows (and updates the
counts) in the sites, trees, woodpieces and slides tables, keeping the
existing metadata. Any `only_ew` and `img_comment` values missing or
`NA` in `rxs_images` are filled from `QWA_meta$images`, so this also
recovers them after a rebuild. Complete any added rows in the metadata
app.

```{r}
QWA_meta <- update_QWAmetadata(QWA_meta, rxs_images)
```

## Combining datasets

Two datasets prepared separately, e.g. from different input folders, can
be combined with `combine_QWAimages()`, `combine_QWAdata()` and
`combine_QWAmetadata()`. Both must have the same ROXAS version and
distinct image labels. Where both contain the same entry (e.g. a shared
site or author), the first object takes precedence. Duplicate-ring flags
are recalculated for woodpiece-years with rings from both datasets.

```{r}
rxs_images <- combine_QWAimages(rxs_images_1, rxs_images_2)
QWA_data <- combine_QWAdata(QWA_data_1, QWA_data_2)
QWA_meta <- combine_QWAmetadata(QWA_meta_1, QWA_meta_2)
```

For example, to build up a dataset one site at a time, run Steps 1--5
of the workflow for each site's folder and combine the `QWAimages` and
`QWAdata` objects. If the metadata app was not used yet, enter the
metadata once for the combined `rxs_images`, so the dataset and author
information is entered only once. Metadata already entered per site is
combined with `combine_QWAmetadata()`.

## Save the updated data

After any of these updates, save the data again:

```{r}
write_QWAimages(rxs_images, "path/to/output_data/example_dataset_QWAimages.csv.gz")
write_QWAdata(QWA_data, dir = path_out, dataset_name = dataset_name, overwrite = TRUE)
write_QWAmetadata(QWA_meta, "path/to/output_data/example_dataset_QWAmetadata.json")
```
